result.title: Clinical value claims in multimodal AI outpace supporting evidence
result.summary: Multimodal prediction models add a data source, such as imaging or an assay, to clinical information, and health systems must decide whether that added test is worth acquiring. We audited 177 studies comparing multimodal with unimodal models: 81 from a systematic review and 96 from a probability sample of 2025-2026 PubMed records. Gains in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) were smaller when a study fitted a separate model for every data source (adjusted difference, -0.030; 95% CI, -0.056 to -0.005). Within 78 such studies, leaving out the strongest source's model would have raised the average gain from 0.046 to 0.108. This complete benchmarking fell from 69.1% of review studies to an estimated 46.0% of recent ones. An estimated 22% assessed decision utility and none evaluated a model prospectively, yet most claimed potential clinical usefulness or improved care (84.0% and an estimated 87.7%).

AI.brief_summary: 该文审计 177 项多模态与单模态临床预测模型对比研究，量化 AUROC 增益与基准做法（是否对每个数据源单独建模、剔除最强来源模型后的增益变化），并统计决策效用评估与前瞻验证的缺失情况。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按数据源消融、以单模态基线衡量模态边际贡献的审计思路，可供核查 LVR 中答案是否真正依用视觉证据、如何量化视觉旁路的贡献，属于方法层面的借鉴线索而非直接竞争。
